extraction.name: PIQA: Physical Interaction: Question Answering
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, consisting of multiple-choice question-answer pairs requiring models to choose the most appropriate solution for a given physical goal. The dataset tests the ability of natural language understanding models to link text to a robust intuitive-physics model of the world, focusing on everyday situations with atypical solutions.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.citeAs: Bisk, Y., Zellers, R., Le Bras, R., Gao, J., & Choi, Y. (2020). PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. arXiv:1911.11641.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through crowdsourced annotations inspired by instructables.com, a platform providing instructions for various tasks. Annotators were given prompts derived from instructables to create goal-solution pairs, with one solution being correct and the other a 'trick' (subtly incorrect). The dataset was cleaned using AFLite to remove annotation artifacts and spurious biases.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Instructables.com, a crowdsourced collection of instructions for tasks ranging from cooking to car repair, providing inspiration for goal-solution pairs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: AFLite algorithm was used to remove stylistic artifacts and trivial examples, discarding instances whose feature representations were highly indicative of the target label. This involved fine-tuning BERT-Large on 5,000 examples and computing embeddings for the remaining instances to identify and remove biased data points.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were asked to provide semantic perturbations or alternative approaches to ensure physical knowledge was targeted. They created goal-solution pairs, with one correct solution and one 'trick' (subtly incorrect). Annotators were free to use linguistic tricks (e.g., negation, numerical changes) or swap key actions/items for topically similar but non-helpful ones. A diff button was included to highlight differences between solutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) for crowdsourcing annotations, with a qualification HIT to ensure annotator quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Examples with low agreement were removed during validation. Annotators achieving >80% accuracy on the qualification HIT were allowed to participate in the main HIT. Data was collected in batches and validated by other annotators for correctness.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 (one correct solution and one 'trick' or incorrect solution per goal)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were selected based on performance in a qualification HIT (>80% accuracy). Annotator pay averaged >$15/hr according to self-reporting and timing calculations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: AFLite (adversarial filtering algorithm) for removing annotation artifacts and biases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to bridge the gap between abstract language understanding and physical commonsense knowledge, which is critical for real-world applications like robotics and human-computer interaction. The lack of physical commonsense in current models highlights the need for further research in this area.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed to minimize reporting bias by encouraging annotators to think creatively and consider atypical solutions. However, initial experiments showed that reporting bias could swamp the dataset, leading to the use of instructables.com as a scaffold to flatten the distribution of referenced objects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses on physical commonsense knowledge, which is inherently limited by reporting bias in language. Models trained on text alone struggle with physical reasoning, as they lack direct experience with the physical world. The dataset may not generalize to domains outside of physical commonsense reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language understanding models. The dataset is intended to evaluate and study the ability of models to capture physical knowledge traditionally experienced in the real world.
